subject: Qualification: PoC plan & deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-corp.com>; Jing Li <jing.li@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T23:02:00Z
Subject: Qualification: PoC plan & deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what Samir, Jing and the team shared: 

Requirements we heard
- Latency target: 50–100ms p95 for user-facing generation flows
- Throughput: ~200 QPS baseline with burst up to 1k for peak events
- Data controls: some PII will be sent to inference endpoints; security/compliance review required (SOC2 + audit logs)
- Residency: primary US region, potential EU data residency for a subset

Recommended PoC path (recommended order)
1) Hosted API 2-week trial (fastest to spin up): validate latency and correctness on a representative workload. Redwood will provide a dedicated trial project, sample prompts, and baseline SLO dashboards.
2) Optional Dedicated capacity smoke test (1 week): if Hosted can't meet latency/throughput, run the same workload on a small Dedicated pool to compare.
3) Private VPC evaluation: if security controls require it after initial validation, move to a Private VPC proof (timeline dependent on procurement & networking).

Success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms under target traffic profile
- Cost: < $X per 1k requests (we'll provide estimates once workload profile is uploaded)
- Quality: end-to-end correctness score >= 92% on the evaluation prompt set
- Security: SOC2 questionnaire answered, evidence for audit-logging enabled

Stakeholders to confirm
- Engineering lead: Jing Li (infra)
- Product/owner: Samir Khan
- Security/compliance: procurement@acme-corp.com (or named person)
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter; Solutions: Marissa Cole

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (PoC tasks & responsibilities)

Ask: can you confirm the stakeholders above and whether you want us to start with Hosted API (recommended) or jump straight to Dedicated/Private? If Hosted works, we can kickoff as early as next week.

Next step: I'll draft a 2-week Hosted PoC plan and send the scope/HubSpot link for approval.

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Price
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
elliot.price@redwood.com

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-corp.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Jing Li <jing.li@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-20T01:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Qualification: PoC plan & deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)

Thanks Elliot — nice summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Security/compliance: we will need SOC2 evidence and a short runbook for audit logging. Our Security lead will want to review the Hosted configuration before we send any PII.
- Preferred path: we are inclined toward Private VPC long-term, but we understand the need to validate model quality and latency first. So yes, start with the Hosted 2-week trial if you can provide guaranteed isolation (project-level) and clear logging.
- Stakeholders: Jing Li (Infra) will lead the technical evaluation; I'll loop in procurement for any paperwork. Contacts: Jing Li <jing.li@acme-corp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-corp.com>
- Timeline: goal is to decide on a deployment mode by end of Q3 and targeted production in Q4. We'd like the PoC to start the week of 2027-06-28 if that works.

On the Dedicated option: if Hosted fails to meet latency under our workload, we'll expect Redwood to provide a short Dedicated smoke test as you suggested. Can you include an estimate of time-to-setup for Dedicated?

—Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Product, Acme Corp
samir.k@acme-corp.com

On Thu, Jun 20, 2027 at 01:14 AM Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Thanks Elliot — nice summary. A few clarifications from our side:
> ...

Samir — thanks for the clarity. A couple of notes from pricing/ops perspective and next steps:

- Hosted trial terms: standard 2-week trial with usage capped to agreed QPS; I'll attach a short scope doc that includes test dataset, metrics, and cancellation terms. (See attachment: acme-poc-scope.pdf)
- Dedicated smoke test: setup time is typically 3–5 business days for a small pool (assuming no extra network policy changes). If you want isolated hardware inside your VPC, that extends time by 2–4 weeks for networking and security approvals.
- Compliance: we'll share SOC2 artifact links and a completed questionnaire within 48 hours after the trial kickoff.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Samir/Jing: confirm kickoff week (you suggested week of 2027-06-28)
2) I'll send the PoC scope & trial terms (DocuSign link included)
3) Elliot/Marissa: schedule a 45-min technical kickoff with Jing + infra on day 1 of the PoC

HubSpot: ACME-2027-0421 (I'll update deal stage to PoC once terms are signed).

Ben Carter

Thanks all — great to see alignment. Confirming plan and next steps: 

Planned PoC (week of 2027-06-28)
- Day 0: paperwork & test dataset upload (Samir/Procurement)
- Day 1: 45-min kickoff (Redwood SE + ACME Infra) — proposed: 2027-06-29 10:00 AM ET
- Days 1–7: Hosted API baseline testing (latency, throughput, correctness) — Redwood provides dashboards and a short eval harness
- Days 8–14: If needed, run small Dedicated smoke test to compare performance

Success criteria (finalized in kickoff)
- p95 latency <= 120ms under target profile
- End-to-end quality >= 92% on the agreed prompt set
- SOC2 evidence reviewed and audit logging validated

Action items
- Samir/Procurement: sign DocuSign trial terms and send test dataset link (Ben will send scope & DocuSign)

If everyone agrees, I'll lock the kickoff for Tue 2027-06-29 10:00 AM ET and send the calendar invite.
